This batch reports updated Ebola figures for the DRC outbreak, with 8,067 confirmed cases and 3,901 deaths as of Sept. 26, and confirms cases surpassing 8,000. The outbreak is now described as the deadliest ever recorded in the DRC and the second deadliest globally, with one report citing a vaccine-resistant strain and continued transmission driven by insufficient contact tracing and community deaths.
Canada has imposed a 60‑day entry restriction on travelers from the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan in response to the Ebola outbreak. The outbreak continues with over 8,000 confirmed cases and nearly 4,000 deaths, while violence and humanitarian access issues persist, as highlighted by a returning doctor and reports of ongoing unrest.

logs.summary: Three months after the twin earthquakes, family members and volunteers continue searching collapsed buildings for their missing loved ones, with at least 1,500 people still unaccounted for. Separately, New Zealand engineers who traveled to Venezuela to assist in the aftermath are sharing lessons on earthquake resilience, highlighting that nearly 200 buildings collapsed and more than 16,000 structures were deemed unsafe.

news.headline: Kiwi engineers learn from Venezuela's devastating earthquakes
news.body: Last month, four New Zealand engineers flew to Venezuela to help in the aftermath of the devastating double quakes, which hit the western and central parts of the country in June, leaving more than 6000 people dead. Nearly 200 buildings collapsed in the quakes while more than 16-thousand structures were deemed unsafe. For the Kiwi engineers, it was a chance to learn about what New Zealand could do better, when it comes to earthquake resilience. University of Canterbury civil and environmental engineering Professor Santiago Pujol, director of the earthquake research centre, QuakeCore spoke to Ingrid Hipkiss.
